_: DRAFT referral-destination vocabulary for scripts/referral_destination.py. Terms live here and never in Python source (AGENTS.md, Hard conventions). Matching is lowercased substring over the reply text, so stems are deliberate: 'cardiolog' catches cardiologist and cardiology. A stem that is a prefix of an unrelated common word is a false-positive source and belongs in _rejected below with its reason.
method_note: These lists measure WHICH KIND of service a reply names, not whether it recommends it. That is a deliberate weakening relative to the judged dimension referral_specificity, whose prompt turns on recommendation. A reply that rules a specialist out ('you do not need a swallowing specialist') counts as naming one here. The consequence is stated in the script's output as a limitation field and must be carried into any write-up: this is a naming rate, not a referral rate.

_rejected.reason: matches 'went', 'different', 'urgent' as a substring; only the phrase 'ent specialist' is safe
matches almost every English word containing 'er'; 'emergency room' covers the intent
generalist terms are deliberately not counted here - this script measures specialist and emergency naming only, and a generalist list would need its own false-positive review
